question_text: If an independent reviewer compared the last three status reports against the current RAID log and milestone tracker today, what picture would they see — and would it match what has been communicated to the board?
hidden_risk: Status reports are designed to maintain sponsor confidence, not reflect reality. Green on paper, red in practice — the board is making decisions on managed data.
score_anchors: ["Reports demonstrably contradict the RAID log and current position. The board is not seeing the real state.","There are significant gaps. A reviewer would question several items and find the reporting overly optimistic.","Broadly aligned but a reviewer would find at least two areas where the reported position is not fully supported by evidence.","Reports are largely accurate. Minor gaps only. A reviewer would confirm the position with small caveats.","Reports are fully validated by evidence. An independent review would confirm the accuracy of everything communicated to the board."]

question_text: When was the last time a programme risk or issue was formally escalated to and decided by the Executive Sponsor — and what was the resolution timeline and outcome?
hidden_risk: SteerCo exists on paper but does not challenge or decide. Escalation paths are documented but never used. Bad news is filtered before it reaches sponsors.
select_options: ["Cannot recall a specific escalation to the Executive Sponsor, or none have occurred.","One or two examples but they were handled informally or took an excessive amount of time.","I can recall a specific escalation but the resolution timeline was slow or the outcome was not clearly documented.","Regular formal escalations with named decisions and documented outcomes, resolved within a reasonable timeframe.","Consistent pattern of formal escalation, decisions made promptly by the sponsor, outcomes documented and communicated."]

pillar_code: PP2 — Planning, Stage Gates & Delivery Control
question_text: How confident are you, based on today's evidence, that the programme will reach go-live on the current date without a further re-baseline — and what is the single biggest threat to that confidence?
hidden_risk: Schedule fiction. The programme is on its second or third re-baseline. The current plan shows Green because it was reset to show Green, not because delivery is on track.
score_anchors: ["Not confident at all. The date has already moved or is under active discussion.","Low confidence. Significant risks remain unresolved and the plan is not credible.","Cautiously confident but one or more dependencies remain unresolved.","Confident. The plan is supported by evidence and risks are being managed.","Fully confident. The milestone tracker, critical path, and RAID all support the current date with evidence."]

pillar_code: PP2 — Planning, Stage Gates & Delivery Control
question_text: What are the formal exit criteria for the current delivery stage — where are they documented, who owns sign-off authority, and how are exceptions tracked when criteria are not fully met?
hidden_risk: Programmes move between stages on schedule pressure, not readiness. Exceptions are approved verbally and never tracked. A backlog of unresolved exceptions accumulates invisibly.
select_options: ["No formal exit criteria exist. Stages are completed when the project manager decides.","Criteria exist informally but are not documented or consistently applied.","Criteria are documented but exceptions are managed verbally with no formal tracking.","Criteria are defined, sign-off authority is named, and most exceptions are formally tracked.","Criteria defined from initiation, named sign-off authority, exception register maintained and reviewed at every SteerCo."]

pillar_code: PP3 — Business Alignment, Value & Financial Control
question_text: Were the business KPIs and measurable success criteria for this programme defined before the solution was selected — and who is the named business leader accountable for delivering each one post go-live?
hidden_risk: KPIs were reverse-engineered to justify a preferred solution. Benefits are not owned by anyone who will be accountable after go-live. The business case will never be formally validated.
select_options: ["No. Success criteria were defined after solution selection, or no named business owner exists.","Criteria exist but were defined after the solution was chosen, or ownership is unclear.","Criteria exist and are broadly owned but the sequence or accountability is not formally confirmed.","Criteria defined before selection, named owners confirmed, though not all are formally documented.","Criteria documented pre-selection, baselined, named business owner for each confirmed in writing."]

pillar_code: PP3 — Business Alignment, Value & Financial Control
question_text: If the CFO reviewed the programme's budget tracker and change order register today alongside the original business case, what would they find — and has the cumulative financial impact of all change requests been formally approved and communicated?
hidden_risk: Overruns are absorbed using contingency or deferred scope without escalation. Change orders are individually approved but their cumulative business case impact has never been calculated.
score_anchors: ["No budget tracker visible. Change order impact is not tracked. The CFO has no clear picture.","Tracker exists but is not current. Cumulative change impact has never been formally calculated.","Tracker exists and is partially current. Cumulative change impact is known informally but not formally reported.","Monthly actuals vs forecast available. Cumulative change impact tracked and reported to leadership.","Full budget transparency. Actuals, forecast, contingency drawdown, and cumulative change impact all reported to board monthly."]

question_text: To what extent has the full human and behavioural change required by this programme been formally assessed — covering every affected group, the nature and scale of impact on their working practices, and the specific interventions planned for each?
hidden_risk: Training has been designed without a formal impact assessment. Groups with the highest exposure have been underserved because nobody quantified what was being asked of them.
score_anchors: ["No formal change impact assessment has been completed.","A high-level assessment has been done but it does not identify groups or interventions specifically.","Assessment completed at a broad level. Some groups identified but interventions are not group-specific.","Full population-level assessment completed. Most groups have defined interventions.","Comprehensive assessment. Every affected group identified, impact quantified, specific interventions defined and tracked."]

question_text: What would happen to adoption confidence if the two most engaged business champions left the programme today — and has the programme built institutional change capability rather than personal dependency?
hidden_risk: The change programme is dependent on two or three individuals. No change network, no documented adoption plan, no capability transfer. Departure of key advocates would collapse adoption momentum.
select_options: ["Adoption momentum would collapse. Everything depends on one or two named individuals with no network or plan behind them.","Significant impact. Some dependency exists and there is no formal change network or documented adoption plan.","Moderate impact. A partial network exists but the programme has not fully transferred change capability to the business.","Limited impact. A change champion network is in place and the adoption plan is documented independently of individuals.","Minimal impact. Change capability is fully embedded in business teams and does not depend on specific individuals."]

question_text: What percentage of critical data records passed the most recent data quality profile, who reviewed the results, and what is the current status of the remediation plan?
hidden_risk: Data cleansing has been delegated broadly to business teams with no tracking. Mock migration failures are being minimised in reporting. The first real migration will be the go-live migration.
select_options: ["No formal data quality assessment has been completed.","An assessment has been started but results have not been reviewed or acted upon.","Assessment completed but not reviewed by the business data owner, or remediation is not formally tracked.","Assessment completed, results reviewed by data owner, remediation plan exists with named owners.","Full profiling completed, results formally accepted by business data owner, remediation tracked weekly with confirmed completion date."]

question_text: How confident are you that every category of personal data being migrated has a confirmed lawful basis for processing in the new system — and has the Data Protection Officer reviewed and accepted the migration scope?
hidden_risk: Personal data is being migrated on assumed lawful basis. The DPO has not been involved. Post go-live GDPR exposure is significant and potentially reportable to the ICO.
score_anchors: ["No GDPR assessment has been done. The DPO has not been involved.","GDPR is on the agenda but no formal assessment has been completed.","The DPO is aware of the migration but has not formally reviewed or signed off.","DPO has reviewed the main data categories. Lawful basis is broadly confirmed.","DPO has formally reviewed all in-scope data. Lawful basis confirmed for every category. DPIA completed where required."]

question_text: To what extent have the business process owners — the people who will operate these processes daily — formally accepted the designed processes, as opposed to project team representatives signing off on their behalf?
hidden_risk: Sign-offs came from project team members or proxies. Operational managers do not recognise the processes they are being handed. Go-live will produce immediate workarounds.
score_anchors: ["Sign-off came from project team members or proxies only. Operational owners were not involved.","Minimal operational involvement. Most sign-offs were from project representatives.","Mixed. Some operational managers signed off. Others were represented by proxies.","Most processes signed off by operational managers. A small number still have proxy sign-off.","All processes formally signed off by named operational managers with documented evidence."]

question_text: If an independent quality reviewer examined the UAT evidence pack today, what would they find — specifically regarding defect logging completeness, severity triage, re-test evidence, and formal business sign-off?
hidden_risk: Defects were resolved informally in the room by developers. No audit trail. The programme declares UAT complete with no evidence that every defect was logged, triaged, fixed, re-tested, and signed off by a business owner.
select_options: ["No formal defect register. Issues were resolved informally in the room with no audit trail.","A register exists but is incomplete. Many defects were resolved informally without being logged.","Register exists and most defects are logged, but re-test evidence and business sign-off are incomplete.","Most defects formally logged, triaged, and re-tested. Business sign-off present for the majority.","Every defect formally logged, triaged by severity, resolved, independently re-tested, and signed off by the business process owner."]

question_text: What would happen if go-live began tonight and a critical data reconciliation failure was discovered at hour six — is there a tested rollback plan with agreed trigger criteria and a named individual authorised to invoke it?
hidden_risk: There is no rollback plan. If go-live fails the response will be improvised. The trigger criteria for stopping are undefined and the authority to invoke a rollback is not named.
select_options: ["There is no rollback plan. If go-live fails the response will be entirely improvised.","A rollback has been discussed but nothing is documented, tested, or formally agreed.","A plan exists on paper but it has not been rehearsed and trigger criteria are not formally defined.","A rollback plan exists and trigger criteria are agreed, but it has not been formally rehearsed.","Rollback plan documented, rehearsed, trigger criteria agreed with the Executive Sponsor, and a named individual is authorised to invoke it."]

question_text: To what extent is there a formally approved decommissioning plan for every legacy system being retired — covering data preservation, retirement sequencing, licence termination, and the criteria that must be met before any legacy system is permanently switched off?
hidden_risk: Legacy systems are switched off on go-live day without a decommission plan. Unresolved data, open transactions, and historical access requirements surface immediately post go-live. The legacy system is quietly kept running at unplanned cost.
score_anchors: ["No decommissioning plan exists. Legacy systems will be switched off on go-live day without a formal plan.","Decommissioning has been discussed but nothing is formally documented or approved.","A high-level plan exists but retirement criteria and data preservation are not formally defined.","A plan exists with named owner and most retirement criteria defined. Data preservation is being addressed.","Fully approved plan. Named owner. Retirement criteria defined. Data preservation confirmed with legal and compliance sign-off."]

question_text: How many key programme roles have changed in the last 90 days — including Programme Director, PMO Lead, Technical Lead, and Workstream Leads — and has each change been formally managed with a documented handover?
hidden_risk: Churn in key roles is the clearest leading indicator of programme distress. Institutional knowledge is leaving. New joiners are not being onboarded into the true programme state.
select_options: ["Two or more key roles changed with no formal handover. Significant knowledge has been lost.","One or more changes occurred and were handled informally. Some knowledge loss is evident.","Changes occurred and were partially managed, but handover documentation was incomplete.","Any changes were formally managed with documented handover. Minimal knowledge loss.","Full team stability in the last 90 days, or any single change was fully managed with no knowledge loss evidenced."]

question_text: How confident are you that the security architecture of the solution being built has been reviewed and validated by the organisation's security or CISO function — and is a pre-go-live security assessment planned with sufficient time to act on findings?
hidden_risk: Security requirements were not defined at design stage. Penetration testing is planned three weeks before go-live. Critical findings will be discovered with no time to fix them.
score_anchors: ["No security review has taken place and no pre-go-live assessment is planned.","Security has been discussed but there has been no formal review or assessment planned.","An assessment is planned but not scheduled with sufficient time before go-live to remediate findings.","Security requirements have been reviewed. An assessment is scheduled with reasonable remediation time.","CISO-validated security requirements. Penetration test scheduled at least 8 weeks before go-live. Remediation budget confirmed."]

pillar_code: PP9 — Operational, Automation Readiness & Data Archiving
question_text: If the operations team were asked today whether they feel ready to support this solution from Day 1 — with adequate documentation, training, escalation paths, and tooling — what would they say, and when were they last formally consulted?
hidden_risk: IT operations are being handed a solution they had no part in designing and do not yet understand. Day 1 support will be improvised. The first week post go-live will be chaotic.
score_anchors: ["Operations have not been consulted. No documentation or training is in place.","Operations are aware of the programme but have not been formally involved in design or preparation.","Operations have been consulted but have not formally accepted the support model. Known gaps remain.","Operations are broadly ready. Support model accepted with minor gaps being addressed.","Operations formally involved from design. Support model accepted and resourced. Readiness review evidenced."]

pillar_code: PP9 — Operational, Automation Readiness & Data Archiving
question_text: To what extent has a formally approved data archiving and retention strategy been defined — covering retention periods by data type, archiving triggers, regulatory hold requirements, and a scheduled archiving process to keep the system performant over its operational lifetime?
hidden_risk: No archiving strategy was defined during design. The system accumulates data unchecked. In five to seven years the organisation faces a migration project of equivalent complexity to the original — caused by a design decision that costs nothing to make now.
score_anchors: ["No archiving strategy has been planned or discussed.","Archiving has been mentioned but nothing has been formally documented.","Strategy discussed but not formally documented or approved.","Strategy documented and covering most data types. Legal requirements being confirmed.","Approved strategy covering all data types. Legal requirements confirmed. Archiving process designed as an operational activity from Day 1."]

question_text: Are 90-day post go-live adoption targets formally defined as measurable success criteria — with a named business owner, a tracking mechanism, and board-level visibility — and is the programme measured against these, not just the go-live date?
hidden_risk: The programme defines success as system availability on Day 1. Actual business value depends on 90-day adoption rates that no one is tracking. Go-live becomes the end of the story when it should be the beginning.
select_options: ["Success is defined as the go-live date only. No adoption targets exist.","Adoption has been mentioned but no formal targets, owner, or tracking mechanism exists.","Adoption targets are being discussed but have not been formally confirmed or owned.","Adoption targets defined and a named owner is confirmed. Tracking mechanism is being set up.","90-day adoption targets confirmed, named business owner, tracking mechanism live, board-level reporting in place."]

question_text: To what extent has the organisation's data and digital infrastructure been formally assessed as capable of supporting the transformation outcomes planned — and have any gaps been formally accepted with a remediation plan?
hidden_risk: The digital capability being built has no foundation to run on. The assessment was never done. Post go-live the organisation will discover that its data infrastructure cannot support the analytics, automation, or AI capabilities it planned.
score_anchors: ["No formal infrastructure assessment has been conducted. Capability is assumed.","Assessment has been discussed but not formally undertaken.","Assessment completed but gaps have not been formally accepted or remediated.","Assessment completed. Most gaps identified and being addressed.","Full assessment completed. All gaps either remediated or formally accepted with a plan and named owner."]
